clue.text: Golf club's weight advantage

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for weight
having the edge means having an advantage

explanation.surface: A golfer reckons a heavier club gives them an advantage on the course.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is': the golf club is W plus EDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedge is a lofted iron used for short approach shots and getting out of bunkers.

clue.text: Spoke quietly with his papa before first of December

indicators.note: first of asks for only the opening letter of the following month name

parts.note: W is a common abbreviation for with
taken as written
Papa is P in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ere is a poetic word for before
the opening letter of December

explanation.surface: A father talked softly to his son ahead of the start of December, perhaps about Christmas presents.
explanation.definitionFit: To whisper is to speak under the breath, so the past tense means talked in a hushed voice.

clue.text: Inside potential clothing store

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping around, so the wanted word sits covered by the letters of the words before it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Reads like a fashion tip about the hidden promise of a clothes shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothing store' looks like a single phrase for a boutique, but clothing is the hiding signal and store alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a warehouse or storehouse where goods are kept.

clue.text: Take out old paper

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-wife
a tract is a short pamphlet or paper on a subject

explanation.surface: Someone is clearing out a stack of old newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract something is to pull or remove it, as a dentist extracts a tooth.

clue.text: Spooner's suggestion for dog is so long

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words, so the starts of two words trade places

parts.note: a suggestion is a tip and the dog is a poodle, so a tip for a poodle; swapping the opening sounds gives the spelling here

explanation.surface: The Reverend Spooner gives some advice about dogs, and it goes on forever.
explanation.walkthrough: A tip for a poodle is POODLE TIP; swapping the P and T sounds gives the old-fashioned farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Toodle-pip is dated British slang for goodbye, just as so long is a casual way of taking leave.

clue.text: The greatest unfinished ancient city

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
the best is the greatest

explanation.surface: A half-built city that was once the finest in the ancient world.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was a major city of ancient Egypt, and also of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Got into bed with a drunk

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone climbed into bed while drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got into bed' reads as one phrase, but Got alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtained and got both mean acquired or came to have something.

clue.text: Missing lounging around topless

indicators.note: topless means without a top, so in a down entry the first letter goes

parts.note: slacking is idling about, avoiding work

explanation.surface: Someone has gone absent, idling about half-dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' is part of the phrase for idling, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking means absent or not present, as in 'something is missing or lacking'.

clue.text: Old-fashioned, demure Italian wives rejecting outsiders

indicators.note: rejecting outsiders means throwing out the outer letters, keeping only the middle

parts.note: prim means demure and proper
IT is the abbreviation for Italian
taken as written

explanation.surface: Traditional, modest Italian wives who keep strangers at arm's length.
explanation.definitionFit: Primitive can mean crude or old-fashioned, belonging to an earlier stage of development.

clue.text: Gem Romeo found in ring

indicators.note: found in places one thing inside another

parts.note: a peal is a ringing of bells
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A jewel turns up in Romeo's engagement ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' suggests jewellery, but here it is the sound of bells.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearl is a precious gem formed inside an oyster.

clue.text: Someone in hospital maybe following this writer is irritated

indicators.note: following places the first word after the second in the answer

parts.note: this writer is the setter, who says I'M for 'I am'
a patient is someone in hospital, the maybe marking an example

explanation.surface: The setter says that someone stuck in hospital behind them is getting annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: There is a neat contrast: a patient becomes impatient once the setter goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Impatient means restless and annoyed at delay, close to irritated.

clue.text: Now breaking tea cups and saucers

indicators.note: breaking into something means entering it, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
in means fashionable, of the moment

explanation.surface: Someone is smashing the tea set right now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' suggests smashed crockery, but it signals putting one word inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: China is porcelain tableware, so cups and saucers are an example of it.

clue.text: Errand boy swallowing too much stew

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: a page is a boy who runs errands
OTT is short for over the top, meaning excessive

explanation.surface: A messenger boy wolfs down far too much stew.
explanation.definitionFit: Pottage is an old word for a thick soup or stew of vegetables and meat.

clue.text: Sign just the first letter

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to mark a document with your letters
second meaning: the opening letter of a name

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one instruction, it tells you to sign with one letter; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to put one's abbreviated signature on a document; as a noun it is the opening letter of a word or name.

clue.text: Returning in shuttle to Mercury? Very unlikely

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters are read from right to left
in tells us the letters are sitting inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word, the whole of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A space shuttle making a return trip to the planet Mercury is hardly likely.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote chance is one that is very unlikely to happen.

clue.text: One who hoards beer keeping bishop depressed

parts.note: a miser hoards money

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted man keeps his beer away from the bishop and is glum about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Miserable means very unhappy, a synonym of depressed.

clue.text: Birds from Portugal sing tune, shivering with temperature dropping

indicators.note: shivering means trembling and shaking, so the letters are shaken into a new order
dropping means letting fall away, so the temperature abbreviation is taken out

parts.note: P is the international vehicle code for Portugal
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: Birds sing as they shiver in the cold, though they hardly belong in Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: Shivering in the cold suits the answer, which helps disguise that it is an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Penguins are flightless seabirds of the southern hemisphere.

clue.text: Prolongs periods inside

definitions.meaning: first meaning: makes something last longer
second meaning: prison sentences, inside being slang for in jail

explanation.walkthrough: Inside is slang for in prison, and a stretch is a term served there.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means extends or lengthens; the noun plural is informal slang for jail terms.

clue.text: Animal prevailed here by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it tells us to go on how the words are spoken, not spelt

parts.note: to reign is to rule or hold sway, so prevailed is reigned

explanation.surface: An animal held sway in this place, or so it sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A reindeer is an Arctic deer, the animal that pulls Santa's sleigh.

clue.text: Heavy blow from attractive person cut flower

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the last letter is chopped off

parts.note: a dish is slang for a good-looking person
the aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: Someone suffers a crushing blow when a beautiful person cuts a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a calamity, a severe blow of misfortune.

clue.text: Red mark on leg finally went for good

indicators.note: for here means in place of, so one letter swaps out another

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word that follows

parts.note: the final letter of went
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A red mark on someone's leg has finally gone for good.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as an instruction, 'finally went for good' puts the last letter of went in place of the G in leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a vivid shade of red.

clue.text: Worry about flipping race

parts.note: care is anxiety or worry

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious about a blooming race.
explanation.walkthrough: Flipping is also British slang meaning 'blooming', which is what the surface uses it as.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to rush headlong at speed, the same as to race.

clue.text: Coat, bra, woolly jumper?

indicators.note: woolly means fuzzy and confused, so the letters become muddled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A list of clothes ending with a woolly jumper, as if packing a suitcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woolly jumper' is a sweater in the surface; the question mark flags that jumper here means someone who leaps. Jumper is the British word for a sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrobat performs leaps and somersaults, so is a kind of jumper in a playful sense.

clue.text: Became needy every now and then supporting clubs?

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting means sitting below, so this piece goes after the other

parts.note: clubs is one of the four suits in a pack of cards

indicators.note: every now and then means only at intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of needy

explanation.surface: Someone occasionally fell on hard times while backing a sports club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Became needy' reads as one phrase, but Became alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Suited can mean looked good on or flattered, as a dress became her.

clue.text: Steal local profit

parts.note: the local is a nearby pub, and a bar is a pub
a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: A thief pockets the takings from the neighbourhood pub.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' means your nearest pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A steal is something bought very cheaply, the same as a bargain.

clue.text: Leaders of British archaeological research body support digs

indicators.note: leaders are the ones at the front, so only the opening letters are taken

parts.note: the opening letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: The heads of a British archaeology institute back excavations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digs' looks like archaeological excavations, fitting the surface, but it means insults.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbs are cutting remarks, and digs are snide jibes of the same kind.

clue.text: Vertical? Just

definitions.meaning: second meaning: honest and morally fair

explanation.walkthrough: Just looks like the adverb 'only', but it is the adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means erect in posture and also honourable in character, as in an upright citizen.

clue.text: Girl isn't so regularly giving smiles

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: A girl is not usually one to smile so much.
explanation.definitionFit: A grin is a broad smile showing the teeth, so the plural is a plain synonym for smiles.

clue.text: Revolutionary piece of fishing equipment catches bream, primarily

indicators.note: catches means holds inside, as a net traps a fish

parts.note: a reel winds the line on a fishing rod

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of bream

explanation.surface: An innovative fishing reel lands a bream first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' seems to praise the reel, and a reel does revolve, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebel is someone who rises against authority, a revolutionary.

clue.text: Found groom his stable

indicators.note: to groom is to tidy and rearrange, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A stable lad is told to groom the horses in his yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past of find, but it is the verb meaning to set up.
explanation.definitionFit: To found an institution is to set it up or establish it.

clue.text: Protected trees held nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Trees that bore nuts were kept safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheltered means shielded from harm or bad weather, a synonym of protected.

clue.text: Hardy girl embracing time trials

indicators.note: embracing means hugging around, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's heroine
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A tough young woman takes on time trials, as in cycling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' looks like the adjective meaning robust, but it is the novelist Thomas Hardy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tests and trials are both examinations of quality or ability.
